integration_status: reviewable upstream patch; not published or pinned by the fereg working tree

kernel_benchmark.description: Source-extracted norm/dot kernels; 100000 entries, one/seven threads, 50 warmups and 2000 timed invocations per block, five alternating pairs. Both arms checked against independent scalar/fixed-point numerical oracles. This is component timing, not command or F0 evidence.

limits: The fix is ready locally but integrating a portable published dependency pin requires authorization to publish the upstream patch. Nothing was pushed or installed.

All 11 final captures pass unchanged exact self-repetition and complete pinned-reference gates. Four previously successful multi-FE controls have intentional last-bit changes relative to the old source; sample, status and DoF remain exact.
No end-to-end before/after performance claim: the affected baseline captures fail their scientific repeat gate. No timing from those failed captures is used as performance evidence.
No F0, RSS, SCC, Windows or release qualification. The frozen exact-extraction policy and capture tolerances remain unchanged.
This bounded repair does not promise bitwise identity for every upstream atomic/preconditioner route or across architectures. Separate explicit-diagonal certificate failures remain open.
temporary_build_overlay_description: Only the isolated candidate snapshot uses Cargo path patches to the source-identified upstream copy. The fereg working tree retains its published git pins and contains no path override.

upstream.mechanism: Set with_max_len(1) on each indexed parallel chunk sum in axpy_with_sq_norm and par_dot. Each 4096-element chunk is one reduction leaf; midpoint splits and left/right addition no longer depend on task stealing. Existing thresholds, per-chunk arithmetic, solvers, certificates and iteration budgets are preserved.

regression_before.description: Identical norm and dot tests fail on the pinned source: one-worker versus nested seven-worker reduction trees differ. Final candidate tests pass at threshold boundaries and long tails.
